children.text: A brackish lake hidden among the limestone cliffs of Coron Island, about
20–30 minutes

by boat from Coron town. Climb a steep staircase to look down on the emerald bay from the viewpoint, then swim and snorkel in the clear lake in a life jacket. It is the signature stop of the Coron Island tour.

Kayangan Lake is a lake hidden deep inside Coron Island in the Calamian Islands of northern Palawan. From Coron town, a bangka (a traditional Philippine boat with bamboo outriggers on both sides) takes about
20–30 minutes

to reach a bay ringed by limestone cliffs like a folding screen, and the lake lies just over the ridge behind it. It is a brackish lake of roughly 70 percent fresh water and 30 percent sea water, and its deepest point is said to be about
. The water is so clear that the rocks and small fish below can be seen straight from the surface, and locals call it "the cleanest lake in Asia."
It is one of the thirteen lakes that the indigenous Tagbanwa people of Coron Island hold sacred. After holding a ritual in
, the Tagbanwa opened Kayangan Lake and Barracuda Lake to visitors, and in

the government recognized their ancestral domain over most of the island. To this day the Tagbanwa community collects the entrance fee, manages the areas and keeps the site clean. The name of the lake is said to come from a Tagbanwa word for a parrot.

A visit goes like this. You step off the boat at the pier and climb a steep stone staircase to the viewpoint, which is the scene that appears most often in photos of Coron. Sharp limestone peaks, an emerald bay and a line of anchored bangkas all come into view at once. Then you go down the stairs on the other side to the lake with its wooden deck, put on a life jacket and get into the water to swim and snorkel.
It is an almost obligatory stop on the Coron Island tour, so it suits travelers who want to take in Coron's scenery in a short time. Since

, when a foreign tourist died while freediving, life jackets have been mandatory, and scuba diving is restricted because of currents. The stairs call for a little fitness, but the lake has shallow areas too, so even weak swimmers can enjoy it in a life jacket.

blocks.title: The bay seen from the viewpoint

children.text: Climb the stairs from the pier to a viewpoint that frames limestone peaks, blue-green water and a row of bangkas in one view. The climb usually takes
5–10 minutes
, and because the photo queue gets long, it is best to go early.

blocks.title: Swimming in the lake in a life jacket

children.text: Step from the wooden deck down the stairs into the water and a cool brackish lake awaits. A life jacket keeps you afloat, so even non-swimmers can float comfortably, and drifting slowly beneath the cliffs feels unique.

Limestone rocks sit under the clear water and schools of small fish drift by. You can see them well even with just a mask, and bringing snorkeling gear lets you watch for longer. Take care not to step on or touch the rocks.

blocks.title: The wooden deck and walking around the lake

children.text: Wooden decks and short walkways run along the edge of the lake, so you can see the lake spreading between the cliffs up close without getting in the water. The deck is slippery when wet, so check the soles of your shoes.

blocks.title: The quiet lake early in the morning

children.text: Around
7 AM
, just after opening, the tour groups have not yet arrived, so you can swim and take photos at ease on the calm lake. At midday, hundreds of people may arrive at once.

Before it is a tourist site, this is a sacred place of the Tagbanwa. Listening to the signs and the explanations of local wardens and moving only within the designated areas will make your trip more meaningful.

blocks.title: Combining it with Barracuda Lake and Twin Lagoon

children.text: Many Coron Island tours also visit Barracuda Lake and Twin Lagoon. Barracuda Lake charges a separate fee of about
, and both places differ from Kayangan in water color and atmosphere, which makes comparing them fun.

items.title: Early-morning half-day route
items.subtitle: For when you want to enjoy the lake before the crowds

children.text: Board a private boat or an early-departure join tour at the Coron town pier. Tell them when you book that you want to leave early in the morning.
Arrive at the Kayangan Lake pier right at opening time, pay the entrance fee of about
and pick up a life jacket.
Climb the stairs and photograph the view of the bay from the viewpoint. The best time is when there is no queue.
Go down to the other side and swim and snorkel in the lake for
40 minutes to 1 hour
Return to the pier before the tour boats arrive in numbers and move on to the next stop. You can continue to Barracuda Lake or Twin Lagoon.

items.title: Full-day Coron Island tour
items.subtitle: A typical full-day route that includes Kayangan Lake

children.text: Go from your lodging to the tour boat pier and board. Most tours include hotel pickup.
Arrive at Kayangan Lake and spend about
1 hour to 1 hour 30 minutes
at the viewpoint and swimming in the lake.
Visit Barracuda Lake or Twin Lagoon (depending on the route). Experience the change in water temperature and swim through the gap in the rocks.
Have lunch cooked on the boat at an island beach or CYC Beach.
Look around snorkeling spots such as the coral gardens and the Skeleton Wreck.
Return to Coron town. Mount Tapyas sunset or Maquinit Hot Spring makes a good follow-up before dark.
The gateway to Coron is Busuanga Airport (USU, Francisco B. Reyes Airport). From Clark, Philippine Airlines, Cebgo (Cebu Pacific group) and Sunlight Air fly several times a day, taking about
1 hour to 1 hour 20 minutes
, and there are direct flights from Cebu as well. Fares vary greatly by season, so count on about
one way.
Since
March 29, 2026

, turboprop operations at Manila's Ninoy Aquino International Airport have stopped, so there are no direct Manila–Busuanga flights. If you leave from Manila, take a P2P bus from NAIA Terminal 3 and elsewhere to Clark Airport (about
2 hours 30 minutes–3 hours
, around
) and then fly, or go via Cebu. Routes change often, so check the latest schedule before booking.
From the airport to Coron town takes about
30–40 minutes
, and a shared van or hotel pickup costs about
per person. It is said that you also pay an environmental fee of about
at the airport on arrival in Coron, so have cash ready.
From Manila, 2GO large passenger ships run about twice a week. The overnight trip takes
12–18 hours
and costs about
depending on cabin class. Timetables change often, so checking is essential.
The fast ferry from El Nido runs a few times a day, takes about
3 hours 30 minutes–4 hours
and costs about
. It is cancelled in bad weather, so leave some slack in your schedule.

items.title: From Coron town to the lake

children.text: Kayangan Lake can be reached only by boat from the Coron town pier. The trip takes about
20–30 minutes
, and most travelers visit on a Coron Island tour that includes hotel pickup and lunch.
Join tours cost about
per person depending on the route, and often include the Kayangan Lake entrance fee, a life jacket and lunch. If you have a group, you can also hire a private boat, with prices starting from about
and rising considerably with the route and group size.
From
November
to
May
is the dry season, with clear skies and calm seas, and the lake looks its prettiest.
December–March

in particular is peak season and the lake can fill with people, so it is best to go right after opening. On days when the northeast monsoon, the amihan, which blows at the same time, is strong, the sea gets rough and tour boats may leave late or be cancelled.
From
June
to
October

is the rainy and typhoon season. On rainy days the stairs are slippery and the lake water can look cloudy, and when a typhoon approaches, sea tours are suspended. On the other hand, there are fewer people and lodging and tour prices drop. Even in the rainy season the mornings are often clear, so scheduling for early hours works well.

There are no lodgings or restaurants at Kayangan Lake itself, so you stay in Coron town. The center near the pier has hostels and guesthouses (about ₱1,250–2,500 per night) and mid-range hotels (about ₱2,500–5,000 per night), which makes early-morning tour departures easy. If you want a quieter getaway you can choose a resort with sea views, but prices rise and the travel time gets longer.

Lunch on a lake tour is usually fish, shrimp and pork bought at the market by the boat crew, grilled over charcoal and served with rice and fruit. Coron town has many seafood restaurants, and some will grill the fish you pick at the market or cook it in chili sauce. There is no shop at Kayangan Lake, so keep drinking water and snacks on the boat. Always take your trash with you.
Tour boats usually crowd Kayangan Lake between
9 and 11 AM
. Booking a route that arrives around the
7 AM
opening time is much more relaxed.
Entry is usually
7 AM to 4 PM
and the entrance fee is about
. Hours and fees can change by community decision, so check the latest information when you book.
The stairs total about
360 steps
up and down, and the stone is slippery. Wear sturdy-soled water shoes or sneakers.
Life jackets are mandatory at the lake. For snorkeling, bring a mask and snorkel or rent them for about
Use sunscreen that protects corals and the lake, and bring a waterproof bag and a towel.
Entrance fees, tips and snacks are often paid in cash. Withdraw from an ATM in Coron town beforehand.
Do not leave trash, and follow the instructions of the Tagbanwa wardens or your guide. It is polite to ask permission before taking photos of people.

Kayangan Lake is sacred Tagbanwa territory. You must follow the on-site rules: wear a life jacket, and no smoking, drinking, littering or stepping on underwater rocks. Fees and operating rules change by decision of the community and local government, so check the latest notice before you visit.
The limestone rocks at the lake are sharp, and rocks underwater can be slippery. Avoid going barefoot or in slippers.
Even in a life jacket, children and weak swimmers must always be watched by an adult. Scuba diving is restricted because of currents, and diving without a life jacket can lead to accidents.
The sun is strong and shade is scarce during the day. Take particular care against heat and ultraviolet rays between
10 AM and 3 PM
and drink water often.
On days with typhoons or monsoon winds, boat trips are cancelled or times change. It is safer not to schedule a tour on the day before your flight home.
The viewpoint stairs and the deck are very slippery when wet. Do not push yourself on rainy days and follow your guide's judgment.
It is about
20–30 minutes
by boat from Coron town to the lake. It is the base from which you can enjoy Barracuda Lake, Twin Lagoon, wreck diving and the Mount Tapyas sunset in one place.
An island south of Coron that was home to the world's largest leprosy colony in the early 20th century. A good day trip when you want to feel history and a quiet island atmosphere.
A wildlife sanctuary in the north of Busuanga Island where you can see giraffes and zebras. It takes more than half a day from Coron town by car and boat.
A resort of limestone cliffs and lagoons about
3 hours 30 minutes–4 hours
away by fast ferry. Many travelers combine it with Coron on a tour of northern Palawan.
